questions.q: What are the three default views shown above the application tree in the Application Navigator?
options: All, Favorites, and History
Recent, Pinned, and Shared
Modules, Tables, and Forms
Admin, User, and Guest
questions.explain: The navigator's top row of views is All, Favorites, and History (with Workspaces appearing once configured).

questions.q: What is a module, in ServiceNow terms?
options: A separate database engine for each application
A saved link inside an application pointing to a specific list or form configuration
A type of user role
A standalone mobile app
questions.explain: Modules are saved links — most point at a list view of a table with a particular filter already applied.

questions.q: When you type "inc" into the Application Navigator filter box, what happens?
options: Nothing changes until you press Enter
Only the Incident application's modules are shown
The tree narrows live to any application or module whose name contains those letters
The instance opens a search results page in a new tab
questions.explain: The filter matches live against both application names and module names at once, not just the Incident application.

questions.q: What does typing "incident.list" into the Application Navigator's filter box and pressing Enter do?
options: Opens a new, blank incident form
Deletes the Incident application from the navigator
Opens the incident table's list view directly, with no saved module required
Adds "incident" to your Favorites automatically
questions.explain: The <table>.list direct-navigation shortcut jumps straight to that table's list view, bypassing the module tree entirely.

questions.q: Why would an admin use the direct-navigation shortcut instead of browsing the Incident application's modules?
options: It is the only way to view the incident table at all
It works for any table you have access to, including ones with no module pointing at them, and skips whatever filter a module applies
Modules cannot open list views, only forms
The shortcut requires administrator role while browsing modules does not
questions.explain: The shortcut is faster for inspecting a table directly and works even for tables that have no module link at all.
